title: Triton
description: Opinionated optimization and QOL modpack for clients and servers
body:
# Triton
Triton is a modern, opinionated QOL & optimization focused modpack, mainly meant for survival gameplay.

## Why "opinionated"?
Triton is meant to be a plug&play experience, with as little further configuration as possible required after installation to get to a good Minecraft experience.
This is why lots of features are included out-of-the-box. If you're looking for a minimal modpack purely focused on performance, try [Fabulously Optimized](https://modrinth.com/modpack/fabulously-optimized).

## Features

<details>
<summary>⚡ General optimization</summary>

Thanks to performance mods like Sodium and Lithium, Triton may improve performance both in clients and servers.

In the same world and on the same system with default settings in both scenarios, Triton provides a ~150 fps increase compared to vanilla Minecraft.

![Triton vs Vanilla FPS comparison. The image shows the identical game scenario in both instances, with 389 fps on Vanilla Minecraft and 535 fps on Triton.](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/28b5a4abb6e7563575ca7fde2ac90fb1d46ffed3.png)

</details>

<details>
<summary>🧭 OptiFine parity</summary>

Most OptiFine features, such as Better Grass, Dynamic Lighting, capes, custom resource pack features, shaders and more are available on Triton.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎤 Voice Chat</summary>

Voice chat through [Simple Voice Chat](https://modrinth.com/plugin/simple-voice-chat) is included. When joining a world or server for the first time, you will get prompted through chat to configure your audio settings.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🗺️ World & mini maps</summary>

A [minimap](https://modrinth.com/mod/xaeros-minimap) and a [world map](https://modrinth.com/mod/xaeros-world-map) are included thanks to Xaero's mods. **Please note that the Cave Mode and Entity Radar features are disabled by default for fairer play, but they can be re-enabled in singleplayer or if the server allows it.**
</details>


<details>
<summary>✨ UI Improvements</summary>

This list is non-exhaustive.

- Smoother scrolling, item, and player animations.
- Dark mode by default
- The XP bar shows both the experience level and Locator Bar at the same time at all times, also replacing colored dots with the players' skins.
- The armor bar changes textures based on the armor you're wearing.
- The hunger bar shows saturation, and each food item shows how much hunger points it recovers in its tooltips.
- You can see your own name in third person and in the inventory.
- View bobbing and hand bobbing are separated, so you can keep your screen still while still seeing the hand bobbing animation.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔨 Utility mods </summary>

This list is non-exhaustive. **Keep server rules in mind when playing multiplayer to avoid getting banned.**

- **Included auto-clicker**: You can set up the in-game autoclicker to AFK at farms. The advantage of having it in-game is that you can do other things on your computer while it is running, and you can set it up to respect the attack cooldown.
- **Freecam**: You can freely move your player camera to view builds from a higher angle.
- **[Tweakeroo](https://modrinth.com/mod/tweakeroo) and Fullbright**: The fullbright tweak in Tweakeroo is bound by default to Ctrl + G.
- **[MiniHUD](https://modrinth.com/mod/minihud)**: By default, you can see your coordinates and IGT in the bottom-left corner, but MiniHUD can be configured to do much more. Check its page for more info.
- **[Litematica](https://modrinth.com/mod/litematica)**: Litematica is installed by default, and the tool item is disabled.
- **In-game calculator**: A calculator can be accessed through the `/calc` command in chat, and it also has some handy tools for Minecraft, like `/calc itemtostack`.

</details>

## Keybinds
| Action               | Key      |
|----------------------|----------|
| VC settings          | Ctrl + V |
| Mute VC              | Ctrl + M |
| Autoclicker config   | Ctrl + O |
| Toggle autoclicker   | Ctrl + I |
| Toggle Freecam       | F4       |
| Zoom                 | C        |
| HD screenshot        | F9       |
| Toggle Fullbright    | Ctrl + G |
| New Waypoint         | B        |

## Set up a Triton server
While Triton works perfectly fine client-side only, creating a server with it can unlock features such as Voice Chat for your players, and optimize it as well. Even after installing Triton on your server, Vanilla players will be able to join as well.

<details>
<summary>Option 1 (recommended)</summary>

If your hosting platform or panel has a way to install Modrinth modpacks directly, use that for the best experience.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Option 2</summary>

If you're self-hosting or your hosting platform doesn't support Modrinth modpack installs directly, the next best option is using **packwiz-installer-bootstrap**. Keep in mind that this option can only install the latest version of the modpack.

After you've set up your Fabric server, follow this guide to install Triton:

- Make sure you have a supported version of Java 25+ installed.
- Download the latest release of `packwiz-installer-bootstrap` from [here](https://github.com/packwiz/packwiz-installer-bootstrap/releases/download/v0.0.3/packwiz-installer-bootstrap.jar) and place it in the root of your server folder.
- Run this command in any terminal, not your MC server console: `java -jar packwiz-installer-bootstrap.jar -g -s server https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alexciao/triton/refs/heads/master/pack.toml`
- Run your server as normal.

</details>
